title: Add descriptions to all --help option lines
description:
## Problem

Every option in `vacuum --help` has a blank description:

```
Options:
      --include <GLOB>  
      --exclude <GLOB>  
      --no-follow       
      --no-witness      
```

Discovered during the spring11 CRE appraisal extraction session. An agent (or human) trying `vacuum --help` as first step gets zero guidance on what the flags do. The `--describe` JSON compensates (it has proper descriptions in operator.v0), but `--help` is the universal first touch.

## Expected

```
Options:
      --include <GLOB>   Include only files matching this glob (repeatable)
      --exclude <GLOB>   Exclude files matching this glob (repeatable)
      --no-follow        Do not follow symlinks
      --no-witness       Suppress witness ledger recording
```

## Notes

- vacuum 0.1.0
- clap derives help from doc comments — likely just missing `/// ...` on the struct fields
- The `--describe` operator.v0 JSON already has the correct text, so it exists — just needs wiring to clap
acceptance_criteria: 1. All options in vacuum --help have non-empty descriptions. 2. Descriptions match the text in --describe operator.v0 JSON. 3. Implemented via clap doc comments (/// ...) on struct fields.
close_reason: Added doc comments to all CLI struct fields — --help now shows descriptions for all options, arguments, and witness subcommands. All 157 tests pass.

title: Enforce root-containment on symlink traversal by default in vacuum
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
- `src/walk/walker.rs:36-38, 127-132`: `vacuum` follows symlinks by default (`!cli.no_follow`) and canonicalizes `record.path` to whatever target the symlink points to — even targets completely outside the scanned root directory.

## Impact
On untrusted data drops or inside a `veil` workflow, a symlink inside `./inbox` pointing to a protected host file silently enters the `vacuum | hashbytes | lock` manifest pipeline and gets hashed/locked.

## Fix
Canonicalize each scanned root and verify that symlink targets stay within that root (emitting a skipped record with an explicit `E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE` warning when a symlink escapes root). Add an opt-in `--allow-outside-root` flag only if cross-root symlinks are explicitly desired.
acceptance_criteria:
- Symlinks pointing outside the scanned root are skipped with a deterministic warning by default (never silently resolved into manifest records).
- In-root symlinks continue to work cleanly.
- Regression test verifies an out-of-root symlink is caught and skipped by default.
close_reason: Re-verified after my failed verification (see my earlier comment: the 36e2483 walker dropped every entry after an escaping symlink in readdir order). Fix 1aa6547 (Lane D; origin main 05a2d80 with CI green) verified by orchestrator: whole suite on an exact export of origin/main, vacuum's own target: 196 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (193 before, 3 new tests). Diff scan of 1aa6547: no assertions removed, no #[ignore] or #[allow] added, Cargo.toml untouched. My exact reproductions, run against BOTH the old binary (from fca77b0) and the fixed one: trees where the escaping link precedes plain files in readdir order (esc_file_rel then data.csv; data1.csv, esc_file_rel, data.csv; esc_file_abs then data.csv; in_root_link, esc_file_abs, data.csv, sub) and my first hostile tree (relative, absolute, directory and nested escaping links, in-root links, a self-referencing loop): OLD binary emitted only 1-2 records and silently lost data.csv and sub/inner.csv; FIXED binary emits every plain file and every link: each escape (file relative/absolute, directory, nested) is a _skipped record with E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE, the loop is a _skipped record with E_IO, in-root links resolve normally; escaped records carry null bytes_hash and null size; the outside files' content never appears in stdout or stderr; output is sorted by relative path and identical across runs; exit 0; --no-follow still lists the links as plain entries; a control with the escape link last in readdir order still lists everything. The pane's regression test multiple_escaping_symlinks_do_not_drop_following_files uses several plain files and three escape kinds and asserts sorted output. NOT verified: Windows symlink semantics, GitHub release builds, downstream hashbytes/lock/pack behavior on escaped-link records, whether the new integration test fails on 36e2483 when run by me (I verified the old behavior with my own reproductions and the pane reports it reproduced the failure before fixing), clippy and ubs locally.

comments.author: zac
comments.text: Implemented and pushed symlink root-containment hardening in commit 36e2483. Followed symlinks are now canonicalized and constrained to the scanned root; an escaping link is represented as _skipped with warning code E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE and is never hashed/locked. In-root links retain normal behavior. The warning is per-entry operational evidence, not an exit-2 refusal, so E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE is intentionally not added to operator refusals. Added a Unix planted-negative test for an escaping symlink; updated README/docs/PLAN. Vacuum spine-rules pin: 76c87d81cddc6ee4939a553ec1efcd0a59c89a5e. Exact commands/results: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo fmt --check (PASS); CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo test --lib walk::walker (PASS, 15 tests); CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo test --test core_scanner symlink_modes_and_skipped_record_contract_hold (PASS, 1 test); CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo test --lib (PASS, 37 tests); CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo test --test golden_rules (PASS, 9 tests); CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings (PASS); git diff --check (PASS); ubs README.md docs/PLAN.md src/walk/walker.rs (completed, 0 critical findings, 97 heuristic warnings, 32 info items). Did not verify GitHub Actions/release builds, cross-platform/Windows symlink semantics, or downstream hashbytes/lock/pack behavior for escaped-link records; did not run the full unfiltered cargo test suite.

comments.author: zac
comments.text: ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION FAILED (stays open; do not release vacuum). The suite passes (193 tests, 0 ignored, CI green at fca77b0) and the single-escape case works, but the root-containment code DROPS EVERY DIRECTORY ENTRY THAT COMES AFTER AN ESCAPING SYMLINK IN READDIR ORDER: exit 0, no warning for the dropped entries, they are simply absent from the manifest. Reproduced on a snapshot of the vacuum built from origin/main fca77b0 (vacuum 0.5.1), several trees, each with plain files and ONE escaping symlink (target outside the scanned root): readdir order esc_file_rel, data.csv (ls -f order) => vacuum emits only esc_file_rel(_skipped) and data.csv is missing; readdir order data1.csv, esc_file_rel, data.csv => emits data1.csv and the skip, data.csv missing; readdir order data.csv, m_esc (escape last) => both emitted, which is why the pane's test and the first trees looked fine; 6 plain files + escape last => all 7 emitted. Plain file with no escaping link => always complete. The released vacuum 0.5.0 lists everything (it has no containment). So the walker aborts the traversal (looks like an early return or break on the escape instead of emit-skip-and-continue), and the result depends on filesystem readdir order (APFS hash order here), so it is also non-deterministic across machines, violating the acceptance 'skipped with a deterministic warning ... never silently'. A silently incomplete manifest feeds hashbytes and lock, which would then seal an incomplete dataset. Exact reproduction (zsh/bash): mkdir -p t/outside t/root; printf S > t/outside/secret.txt; printf a > t/root/data1.csv; printf b > t/root/data.csv; ln -s ../outside/secret.txt t/root/esc; ls -f t/root (note the order: the failure needs a plain file AFTER esc in this listing; create names until it holds, e.g. esc_file_rel then data.csv); vacuum t/root --no-witness | jq -r .relative_path. Needed: (1) find the abort in src/walk/walker.rs (every skip path, not only E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE: also the unreadable/loop 'Cannot read' skip) and make each emit the _skipped record and CONTINUE; (2) also make the output order deterministic (sorted by relative path) so the manifest does not depend on readdir order, if it is not already sorted after collection; (3) a planted-negative test that is NOT order-lucky: e.g. a unit test on the walker's entry handler with the escaping entry first, plus an integration test with several plain files and several escaping links, asserting every plain file is present and every escape is a _skipped record with E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE; the test must fail on 36e2483; (4) whole suite + clippy + a NEW evidence comment. No Cargo.toml version change.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
Repair evidence

Reproduced the orchestrator failure before the fix on the vacuum 0.5.1 source: created /tmp/vacuum-bd3yk.nCIQp5/root with esc_file_rel before data.csv in ls -f order, then ran CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo run -- /tmp/vacuum-bd3yk.nCIQp5/root --no-witness. The scan exited 0, emitted data1.csv and esc_file_rel as _skipped E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE, and silently omitted data.csv. This confirmed the readdir-order-dependent early skip in 36e2483.

Fix pushed as 1aa6547 (rebased onto upstream verification-failure commit 2e900c7). src/walk/walker.rs now has a per-entry handler and one append/report path for normal, E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE, and WalkDir Cannot read records. File escapes never call skip_current_dir; escaping directories do, preventing traversal without dropping later siblings. Existing final JSONL serialization already sorts by relative_path then root; the new integration test asserts the complete output remains sorted. No Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock version change; bd-8bv was untouched.

Planted negatives and exact commands/results: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo test --lib walk::walker -- --test-threads=1 passed 17; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo test --test core_scanner multiple_escaping_symlinks_do_not_drop_following_files -- --test-threads=1 passed 1; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo fmt --check passed; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo test passed 192 tests with 0 failed and 0 ignored; ubs src/walk/walker.rs tests/core_scanner.rs passed with 0 critical findings, 278 warnings, and 73 info; git diff --check passed. The integration test creates relative-file, absolute-file, and directory escapes before three plain files, requires every plain file, requires every escape as _skipped with E_SYMLINK_ESCAPE, asserts all three outside canaries are absent from stdout, asserts no output path starts under the outside root, and asserts sorted relative paths.

Not verified: GitHub Actions or release builds, Windows symlink semantics, and downstream hashbytes/lock/pack execution over escaped-link records. Bead remains in progress; never closed.

title: CLI smoke tests matching pack pattern
description: Build release binary, run vacuum --version, --describe, --schema, vacuum on test fixtures, verify JSON output parses, verify exit codes for refusal paths. Can be standalone script or part of CI smoke job.

title: PRM-VAC-0003: Recursive walker + symlink behavior
description:
Implement recursive directory traversal with walkdir and symlink behavior from plan.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scans one or more roots recursively and collects file entries.
- Default follows symlinks; --no-follow disables symlink-directory traversal and uses link metadata semantics.
- Symlink cycles do not crash scan.

## Notes
Boundary: entry collection only; filtering/sorting/output in downstream beads.
close_reason: Completed: implemented recursive multi-root walkdir scanning, follow/no-follow symlink behavior, cycle-safe traversal, and walker unit tests

title: Suggest a parent directory when vacuum receives a file path
description:
## Scope
Improve the refusal when vacuum is given a file path instead of a directory.

## Deliverables
- keep the refusal outcome for file paths
- include a next_command that suggests scanning the parent directory or current directory
- keep wording consistent with vacuum's contract: enumerate directories, not single files

## Out of Scope
- adding per-file manifest mode
- changing scan semantics to accept arbitrary files
- changing downstream JSONL shape

## Acceptance Criteria
- passing a file path returns a refusal with a non-null next_command
- suggested remediation points at the parent directory or .
- regression coverage includes the file-path misuse case
close_reason: Released in v0.3.2 after adding parent-directory remediation for file-path misuse.

title: Run doctor-mode audit and add read-only vacuum doctor
description: Run world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools against vacuum in audit-first mode, then implement the first safe read-only doctor surface. Expected surface: vacuum doctor health, vacuum doctor capabilities --json, vacuum doctor robot-docs, and vacuum doctor --robot-triage or equivalent. Scope first slice to detection, scoring, robot docs, and tests. Do not add fix mode until the vacuum-specific failure-mode inventory has detector, backup, inverse, and fixture coverage. Acceptance: skill workspace artifacts or databook attached, repo-specific failure modes captured as follow-up beads, quality gate green, ubs on changed files, and br sync --flush-only.
notes: Release gate: after the doctor slice is implemented, cut the repo's normal release only if the implementation is tested, CLI smoke checks pass, and behavior is clearly non-breaking. If tests are weak, behavior is ambiguous, or operator judgment/open questions are required, hold the release and file/update a follow-up bead documenting the blocker.
close_reason: Implemented read-only vacuum doctor upgrade with audit workspace, tests, quality gates, DataBook emission, and release gate.

title: Stream blake3 output hashing while printing JSONL lines in vacuum
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
- `src/lib.rs:96-105` concatenates every serialized JSONL line into a single `output_bytes: Vec<u8>` allocation solely to call `blake3::hash(&output_bytes)`.

## Fix
Update a streaming `blake3::Hasher` as each line is written to stdout (zero duplicate full-output allocation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Witness `output_hash` is computed via streaming `blake3::Hasher` with byte-identical digest to the previous implementation.
- Full-output `Vec<u8>` concatenation is removed.
